# ReFEFF WASI dependency notices

`RUST-NOTICES.txt` preserves 163 license, COPYING and NOTICE files for the 96
packages selected by ReFEFF's `refeff-cli` normal/build dependency graph for
`wasm32-wasip1`. Identical file bytes appear once in 55 sections. The accompanying
`rust-dependencies.json` records every package, declared license, source file,
checksum and byte offset into the text bundle.

The source is ReFEFF commit
[`91b23364309c3daca871b748ae45bf2426c60b8e`](https://github.com/Ameyanagi/refeff/tree/91b23364309c3daca871b748ae45bf2426c60b8e),
which builds the ReFEFF 0.4.0 browser distribution with `refeff-cli` 0.3.0.
The selection follows its [`wasm/build.mjs`](https://github.com/Ameyanagi/refeff/blob/91b23364309c3daca871b748ae45bf2426c60b8e/wasm/build.mjs)
package and target, using the committed `Cargo.lock`.

This is a conservative attribution inventory: it includes build dependencies
and procedural macros, and does not establish which packages contribute bytes
to the final WebAssembly. Cargo dev-only dependencies are excluded. Rust
standard-library/compiler-runtime and WASI libc components are outside this
Cargo-package inventory. The website also retains the upstream ReFEFF/FEFF10
license, upstream notice and browser WASI shim licenses separately.

The generator reads the six ReFEFF workspace crates from a clean Git archive.
For the 90 registry crates, it verifies each `.crate` archive against `Cargo.lock`
before reading its manifest and notice files. Twelve packages omit their primary
license text from the crate archive: `equator` 0.2.2, `equator-macro` 0.2.1,
`faer` and `faer-traits` 0.24.0, `nano-gemm` 0.2.2, six `nano-gemm-*` 0.2.1
packages, and `pulp-wasm-simd-flag` 0.1.0. Their upstream repository-root licenses
are retained from the exact VCS commits recorded inside those crate archives.
The inventory identifies these supplemental URLs and hashes. No selected Cargo
package remains without a retained license text.

To regenerate, use Python 3.12+, Git, Cargo compatible with the upstream manifest,
and a local ReFEFF repository containing the pinned commit:

```sh
uv run --no-project --python 3.12 website/scripts/generate-refeff-notices.py \
  --refeff-repository ../refeff
```

Add `--check` to compare the generated bytes with the retained files. The command
does not change the ReFEFF checkout or rebuild WebAssembly. Cargo may download
locked registry archives; supplemental notice URLs are checksum pinned. Regular
website builds copy and verify these checked-in outputs without running Cargo
metadata or downloading their license sources.

License file bytes are unchanged, including whitespace. The generator adds only
section labels and an introduction, and records exact byte boundaries so the
original texts can be recovered and their hashes verified.

## Bundled runtime notices

The published WebAssembly's `producers` section identifies Rust 1.95.0 at
`59807616e1fa2540724bfbac14d7976d7e4a3860` and clang 21.1.4 from WASI SDK.
`TOOLCHAIN-NOTICES.txt` retains the corresponding Rust, compiler-builtins and
WASI libc notices. `rust-COPYRIGHT-library.html` is Rust's complete, unchanged
standard-library notice, extracted from the official Rust 1.95.0 archive after
checking its published SHA-256 digest. These files supplement the Cargo
inventory above.

`toolchain-provenance.json` records the observed producers, immutable source URLs,
source and archive hashes, retained byte ranges and bundle offsets. That Rust
revision's distribution Dockerfile selects WASI SDK 30, whose submodule records
identify WASI libc `ec0effd769df5f05b647216578bcf5d3b5449725`. The official Rust
WASI sysroot archive contains `dlmalloc` and `fts` objects; the related upstream
notices are retained. The alternative `emmalloc` allocator is absent from that
archive. This traces the runtime distribution and its source notices without
claiming a complete map of the functions linked into ReFEFF.

Runtime notices are retained directly from the recorded sources; the Cargo
notice generator does not regenerate them. To refresh them, fetch the recorded
immutable source files or release archives, verify their hashes, and copy the
recorded byte ranges or archive members unchanged. The dlmalloc notice is the
license/version preamble before its source file's `Quickstart` section; all
other retained source notices are complete files.
